label: Why was the horse led out of the stable instead of being harmed in it?
quote: Why should he take the horse out of the stable? If he wished to injure it why could he not do it there?

possibilities.value: something else
to carry him off and hide him
to hand him over to the gypsies
possibilities.quote: might he not have been leading the horse to them when he was overtaken

possibilities.value: to do something to him that could not be done in the stall

reasoning.text: A man who only wanted the favourite lamed could have done it in the stall. Leading him a quarter-mile onto the moor at night suggests something that needed open ground or no witnesses close by.

possibilities.value: whoever led him out was not Simpson but someone who could open the door

reasoning.text: No duplicate key has been found. The door was locked, and the trainer had his own key and went out at one.

label: Where did the powdered opium come from?

possibilities.value: something else
brought from London
possibilities.quote: The opium was probably brought from London.

possibilities.value: bought from a chemist in the district

reasoning.text: Holmes asks which chemist sold it. Whoever drugged the curry may have bought it locally, and a sale could be traced.

possibilities.value: from someone at the trainer's house

reasoning.text: Only Hunter's portion of the curry held opium, so it may have been added before the dish left the house, by someone who had it there.

reasoning.text: Nothing yet links them to Simpson or the horse. A camp near a murder has reason enough to move off, and the reward puts the gypsies on the side of finding the horse (¶37).
